studies.title: Effect of an alpha-melanocyte stimulating hormone analog on penile erection and sexual desire in men with organic erectile dysfunction.
studies.abstract: To assess the safety, erectogenic properties, and effect on sexual desire of Melanotan II, a synthetic melanotropic initiator of erection, in men with erectile dysfunction and organic risk factors. Ten subjects were enrolled in a double-blind, placebo-controlled, crossover study. Melanotan II (0.025 mg/kg) and vehicle were each administered twice by subcutaneous injection; real-time RigiScan monitoring and a visual analog were used to quantify the erections during a 6-hour period. The level of sexual desire and side effects were recorded with a questionnaire. Melanotan II initiated subjectively reported erections in 12 of 19 injections versus only 1 of 21 doses of placebo. The mean rigidity score of the responders was 6.9 on a scale of 0 to 10. The mean duration of tip rigidity greater than 80% was 45.3 minutes with Melanotan II versus 1.9 for placebo (P = 0.047). The level of sexual desire after injection was significantly higher after Melanotan II administration than after placebo. Nausea and stretching/yawning occurred more frequently with Melanotan II, and 4 of 19 injections were associated with severe nausea. The erectogenic properties of Melanotan II are not limited to cases of psychogenic erectile dysfunction; men with a variety of organic risk factors developed penile erections. The finding of increased sexual desire warrants further investigation of centrally acting agents on disorders of sexual desire.

studies.title: Melanocortin receptor agonists, penile erection, and sexual motivation: human studies with Melanotan II.
studies.abstract: We review our experience with Melanotan II, a non-selective melanocortin receptor agonist, in human subjects with erectile dysfunction (ED). Melanotan II was administered to 20 men with psychogenic and organic ED using a double-blind placebo-controlled crossover design. Penile rigidity was monitored for 6 h using RigiScan. Level of sexual desire and side effects were reported with a questionnaire. In the absence of sexual stimulation, Melanotan II led to penile erection in 17 of 20 men. Subjects experienced a mean of 41 min Rigiscan tip rigidity>80%. Increased sexual desire was reported after 13/19 (68%) doses of Melanotan II vs 4/21 (19%) of placebo (P<0.01). Nausea and yawning were frequently reported side effects due to Melanotan II; at a dose of 0.025 mg/kg, 12.9% of subjects had severe nausea. We conclude that Melanotan II is a potent initiator of penile erection in men with erectile dysfunction. Our findings warrant further investigation of melanocortin agonists and antagonists on penile erection. International Journal of Impotence Research (2000) 12, Suppl 4, S74-S79.

studies.title: Synthetic melanotropic peptide initiates erections in men with psychogenic erectile dysfunction: double-blind, placebo controlled crossover study.
studies.abstract: We evaluated the erectogenic properties of a new cyclic alpha-melanocyte-stimulating hormone analogue, Melanotan-II, to treat men with psychogenic erectile dysfunction. Ten men with erectile dysfunction of no known organic cause were entered in a double-blind, placebo controlled crossover study in which the erectogenic properties of Melanotan-II and a vehicle placebo were compared using real-time RigiScan monitoring. The presence, duration and rigidity of erections were recorded during a 6-hour period. In 8 of 10 men treated with Melanotan-II clinically apparent erections developed. Mean duration of tip rigidity greater than 80% was 38.0 minutes with Melanotan-II and 3.0 with placebo (p=0.0045). Transient side effects of nausea, stretching and yawning, and decreased appetite were reported more frequently after injections of Melanotan-II than placebo but none required treatment. Melanotan-II is a potent initiator of erections in men with psychogenic erectile dysfunction and has manageable side effects at a dose of 0.025 mg./kg.

studies.title: Melanotan Tanning Injection: A Rare Cause of Priapism.
studies.abstract: Melanotan II, an injectable melanocortin analog, is illicitly available on the internet to generate a sunless tan through melanocyte induction. It is also used as a sexual stimulant in unlicensed performance enhancement clinics, and has been investigated as a possible treatment agent in erectile dysfunction. We describe in this case report a patient presenting with acute ischemic priapism after subcutaneous injection of melanotan II. The patient was initially managed with cavernosal aspiration and irrigation, and intracavernous injection of phenylephrine without achieving detumescence. After failing initial management, the patient underwent operative management with penoscrotal decompression, a promising alternative technique for the management of refractory ischemic priapism. Priapism after melanotan II injection has only been reported in the literature twice before. This case report highlights a rare presentation of acute ischemic priapism after melanotan II use, managed with surgical decompression. Future therapeutic applications of these agents and updated management guidelines should consider priapism as a possible side effect. CW. Mallory, DM Lopategui, BH. Cordon. Melanotan Tanning Injection: A Rare Cause of Priapism. Sex Med 2021;9:100298.

studies.title: Melanotan-II: Investigation of the inducer and facilitator effects on penile erection in anaesthetized rat.
studies.abstract: The effects of melanotan-II, a non-specific agonist of melanocortin receptors, on erection and its possible sites of action were investigated in anesthetized rats. Delivered i.v. (0.1, 0.3 and 1 mg/kg) or within the paraventricular nucleus of the hypothalamus (0.1 and 1 microg), melanotan-II exerted a dose-dependent inducer activity on erection by eliciting erectile events and shortening latency of the first erectile event to occur. Erectile events were of higher amplitude in rats treated with melanotan-II i.t. (0.2 microg) delivered at the L6-S1 level than in animals treated with the vehicle i.t. delivered. Erectile responses elicited by cavernous nerve stimulation were increased after i.v. melanotan-II (1 mg/kg), thereby exerting facilitator effect on erection. In contrast, melanotan-II injected within the corpus cavernosum (1 microg) did not display any facilitator activity. To investigate the neural pathways involved in the facilitator effect of melanotan-II, we performed acute spinalization (T8 level) and differential selective nerve transections. Neither spinalization nor bilateral transection of pelvic nerves or dorsal penile nerves impaired facilitator activity of i.v. melanotan-II (1 mg/kg). Conversely, the facilitator effect of melanotan-II was abolished after acute removal of the lumbar paravertebral sympathetic chain. These results lead to the conclusion that central and peripheral melanocortin pathways are recruited by melanotan-II, depending on its route of delivery, to exert both inducer and facilitator activities on erection.

studies.title: The use of telemetry technology to test the proerectile effect of melanotan-II (MT-II) in conscious rats.
studies.abstract: The aim of this study is to demonstrate that monitoring, by means of telemetry technology, the increases in intracavernosal pressure (ICP) in freely moving rats using melanotan-II (MT-II) as a proerectile inducer compound is a relevant experimental model to investigate the effects of pharmacological agents on erection. Adult rats were implanted in the corpus cavernosum with a pressure sensor which permitted telemetric monitoring of ICP in freely moving animals following MT-II (0.1, 0.3 and 1 mg/kg) or saline i.v. injections. ICP was also measured after MT-II (0.1, 0.3 or 1 mg/kg) or saline i.v. delivery in anesthetized rats. In conscious rats, MT-II (1 mg/kg) significantly increased overall erectile activity compared to saline. In anesthetized rats, MT-II-induced increase in overall erectile activity was not statistically significant but displayed a similar pattern. The use of telemetry technology allowed to collect quantifiable and reliable data regarding the proerectile activity of MT-II in physiological conditions. The telemetry model appears suitable for investigating the potential inducer proerectile properties of pharmacological agents.

studies.title: Activation of central melanocortin receptors by MT-II increases cavernosal pressure in rabbits by the neuronal release of NO.
studies.abstract: 1. Melanotan-II had been reported to cause penile erections in men with erectile dysfunction. In the present study, we investigated the mechanisms by which systemic administration of MT-II increases intracavernosal pressure in anaesthetized rabbits. 2. MT-II (10 microM) had no effect on electrical field stimulation-evoked relaxations of rabbit corpus cavernosal strips in vitro. 3. Intravenous injection of MT-II (66 and 133 microg kg(-1) elicited dose-related increases in cavernosal pressure. SHU 9119 (3 microg kg(-1), i.v.), a non-selective antagonist of MC(3) and MC(4) receptors did not significantly affect either cavernosal pressure or systemic blood pressure but abolished the MT-II-induced increases in cavernosal pressure. SHU 9119 also inhibited the depressor response produced by MT-II. 4. Intracavernosal injection 100 microl of the cocktail containing phentolamine mesylate (1 mg ml(-1)), papaverine (20 mg ml(-1)) and PGE1 (20 microg ml(-1)) increased the cavernosal pressure by about 4 fold. 5. The role of NO-cyclic GMP dependent pathway to MT-II-induced increases in cavernosal pressure was investigated by bilateral transection of the pudendal nerves and by inhibition of NO synthase with L-NAME (20 mg kg(-1), i.v. over 30 min). Ablation of the pudendal nerves or pretreatment with L-NAME abolished the MT-II-induced increases in intracavernosal pressure in anaesthetized rabbits. 6. The data suggest that activation of central melanocortin receptors by MT-II increases cavernosal pressure by the neuronal release of NO.

studies.title: Melanotan-II reverses autistic features in a maternal immune activation mouse model of autism.
studies.abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a complex neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by impaired social interactions, difficulty with communication, and repetitive behavior patterns. In humans affected by ASD, there is a male pre-disposition towards the condition with a male to female ratio of 4:1. In part due to the complex etiology of ASD including genetic and environmental interplay, there are currently no available medical therapies to improve the social deficits of ASD. Studies in rodent models and humans have shown promising therapeutic effects of oxytocin in modulating social adaptation. One pharmacological approach to stimulating oxytocinergic activity is the melanocortin receptor 4 agonist Melanotan-II (MT-II). Notably the effects of oxytocin on environmental rodent autism models has not been investigated to date. We used a maternal immune activation (MIA) mouse model of autism to assess the therapeutic potential of MT-II on autism-like features in adult male mice. The male MIA mice exhibited autism-like features including impaired social behavioral metrics, diminished vocal communication, and increased repetitive behaviors. Continuous administration of MT-II to male MIA mice over a seven-day course resulted in rescue of social behavioral metrics. Normal background C57 male mice treated with MT-II showed no significant alteration in social behavioral metrics. Additionally, there was no change in anxiety-like or repetitive behaviors following MT-II treatment of normal C57 mice, though there was significant weight loss following subacute treatment. These data demonstrate MT-II as an effective agent for improving autism-like behavioral deficits in the adult male MIA mouse model of autism.

studies.title: The effects of the melanocortin agonist (MT-II) on subcutaneous and visceral adipose tissue in rodents.
studies.abstract: The melanocortin system is a critical pathway in the regulation of energy balance. In this study, we analyzed the peripheral effects of the synthetic melanocortin agonist melanotan-II (MT-II) in rodents fed a low-fat or high-fat diet. MT-II-treated high-fat diet-induced obese (DIO) mice lost weight and body fat, whereas MT-II-treated low-fat-fed mice maintained their original body weight. Specifically, MT-II treatment led to a general reduction in both visceral and subcutaneous adipose tissue in high-fat-fed mice compared with Vehicle (ad libitum) controls. Vehicle-treated pair-fed DIO mice lost an equivalent amount of body weight compared with MT-II-treated mice but retained more adipose tissue. Pair-fed mice showed a reduction in visceral adipose tissue and no effect on subcutaneous adipose tissue compared with MT-II-treated mice. It is surprising that subcutaneous lean mass was significantly reduced in the pairfed mice. The data were replicated in DIO rats and indicated that MT-II treatment led to a generalized reduction in adipose tissue. These results indicate that peripheral MT-II treatment leads to weight loss that affects both the visceral and subcutaneous fat compartments. This finding illustrates the complexity of analyzing weight-reducing compounds. Although the present data suggest that the anorectic effect of MT-II is primarily a consequence of reduced food intake, the body composition data suggest that other mechanisms are involved.
studies.journal: The Journal of pharmacology and experimental therapeutics

studies.title: The melanocortin agonist Melanotan-II reduces the orexigenic and adipogenic effects of neuropeptide Y (NPY) but does not affect the NPY-driven suppressive effec
studies.abstract: Neuropeptide Y (NPY) is a strong orexigenic neurotransmitter also known to modulate several neuroendocrine axes. alpha-Melanocyte-stimulating hormone (MSH) is an essential anorectic neuropeptide, acting on hypothalamic MC3/4 receptor subtypes. When given as an intracerebroventricular bolus injection, Melanotan-II (MT-II), a non selective MC receptor agonist, inhibits feeding, suppresses the NPY orexigenic action, and reduces basal insulinaemia. We evaluated the effects of a 7-day central infusion of MT-II (15 nmol/day) given either alone or in association with NPY (5 nmol/day) in male Sprague-Dawley rats. MT-II produced almost full anorexia for 1-2 days but then feeding gradually returned to normal despite continued MT-II infusion. When coinfused with NPY, MT-II also produced the same initial anorectic episode but then maintained feeding to upper normal levels, thus cancelling the hyperphagia driven by NPY. Whereas NPY infusion produced a doubling of fat pad weight, MT-II reduced adiposity by a factor of two compared to pair-fed rats, and vastly curtailed the NPY-driven increase in fat pad weight. MT-II infusion also significantly curtailed the NPY-induced rise in insulin and leptin secretions. NPY infusion significantly inhibited hypothalamic pro-opiomelanocortin mRNA expression, most likely cancelling the alpha-MSH anorectic activity. As expected from previous studies, chronic NPY infusion strongly inhibited both the gonadotropic and somatotropic axes, and coinfusion of MT-II did not reverse these NPY-driven effects, in sharp contrast with that seen for the metabolic data. MT-II infusion alone had little effect on these axes. In conclusion, chronic MT-II infusion generated a severe but transient reduction in feeding, suggesting an escape phenomenon, and clearly reduced fat pad size. When coinfused with NPY, MT-II was able to cancel most of the NPY effects on feeding, but not those on the neuroendocrine axes. It appears therefore that, as expected, NPY and alpha-MSH closely interact in the control of feeding, whereas the neural pathways by which NPY affects growth and reproduction are distinct and not sensitive to MC peptide modulation.

studies.title: Differential activation of the sympathetic innervation of adipose tissues by melanocortin receptor stimulation.
studies.abstract: Melanocortins are implicated in the control of energy intake/expenditure. Centrally administered melanotan II (MTII), a synthetic melanocortin 3/4-receptor agonist, decreases adiposity beyond that accountable by food intake decreases. Melanocortin-4 receptor (MC4-R) mRNA is expressed on sympathetic nervous system (SNS) outflow neurons to white adipose tissue (WAT) in Siberian hamsters, suggesting a role in lipid mobilization. Therefore, we tested whether third ventricular injections of MTII increased sympathetic drive to WAT and interscapular brown adipose tissue (IBAT) using norepinephrine turnover (NETO) as a measure of sympathetic drive. We also tested for MTII-induced changes in lipolysis-related WAT gene expression (beta3-adrenoceptors, hormone sensitive lipase) and IBAT thermogenesis (beta3-adrenoceptor, uncoupling protein-1). Finally, we tested whether third ventricularly injected MTII, a highly selective MC4-R agonist (cyclo[beta-Ala-His-D-Phe-Arg-Trp-Glu]NH2) increased or agouti-related protein decreased IBAT temperature in hamsters implanted with sc IBAT temperature transponders. Centrally administered MTII provoked differential sympathetic drives to WAT and IBAT (increased inguinal WAT, dorsosubcutaneous WAT and IBAT NETO, but not epididymal WAT and retroperitoneal WAT NETO). MTII also increased circulating concentrations of the lipolytic products free fatty acids and glycerol but not plasma catecholamines, suggesting lipid mobilization via WAT SNS innervation and not via adrenal medullary catecholamines. WAT or IBAT gene expression was largely unaffected by acute MTII treatment, but IBAT temperature was increased by MTII and the MC4-R agonist and decreased by agouti-related protein. Collectively, this is the first demonstration of central melanocortin agonist stimulation of WAT lipolysis through the SNS and confirms melanocortin-induced changes in BAT thermogenesis.

studies.title: Therapeutic Strategies Against Metabolic Imbalance in a Male Mouse Model With 5-HT2CR Loss-of-Function.
studies.abstract: The serotonin 2C receptor (5-HT2CR)-melanocortin pathway plays well-established roles in the regulation of feeding behavior and body weight homeostasis. Dysfunctions in this system, such as loss-of-function mutations in the Htr2c gene, can lead to hyperphagia and obesity. In this study, we aimed to investigate the potential therapeutic strategies for ameliorating hyperphagia, hyperglycemia, and obesity associated with a loss-of-function mutation in the Htr2c gene (Htr2cF327L/Y). We demonstrated that reexpressing functional 5-HT2CR solely in hypothalamic pro-opiomelanocortin (POMC) neurons is sufficient to reduce food intake and body weight in Htr2cF327L/Y mice subjected to a high-fat diet (HFD). In addition, 5-HT2CR expression restores the responsiveness of POMC neurons to lorcaserin, a selective agonist for 5-HT2CR. Similarly, administration of melanotan II, an agonist of the melanocortin receptor 4 (MC4R), effectively suppresses feeding and weight gain in Htr2cF327L/Y mice. Strikingly, promoting wheel-running activity in Htr2cF327L/Y mice results in a decrease in HFD consumption and improved glucose homeostasis. Together, our findings underscore the crucial role of the melanocortin system in alleviating hyperphagia and obesity related to dysfunctions of the 5-HT2CR, and further suggest that MC4R agonists and lifestyle interventions might hold promise in counteracting hyperphagia, hyperglycemia, and obesity in individuals carrying rare variants of the Htr2c gene.

studies.title: Intracerebroventricular administration of melanotan II increases insulin sensitivity of glucose disposal in mice.
studies.abstract: The present study was conducted to evaluate the effects of central administration of melanotan II (MTII), a melanocortin-3/4 receptor agonist, on hepatic and whole-body insulin sensitivity, independent of food intake and body weight. Over a period of 24 h, 225 ng of MTII was injected in three aliquots into the left lateral ventricle of male C57Bl/6 mice. The animals had no access to food. The control group received three injections of distilled water. Whole-body and hepatic insulin sensitivity were measured by hyperinsulinaemic-euglycaemic clamp in combination with [(3)H]glucose infusion. Glut4 mRNA expression was measured in skeletal muscle. Plasma glucose and insulin concentrations under basal and hyperinsulinaemic conditions were similar in MTII- and placebo-treated mice. Endogenous glucose production (EGP) and glucose disposal in the basal state were significantly higher in MTII-treated mice than in the control group (71+/-22 vs 43+/-12 micromol.min(-1).kg(-1), p<0.01). During hyperinsulinaemia, glucose disposal was significantly higher in MTII-treated mice (151+/-20 vs 108+/-20 micromol.min(-1).kg(-1), p<0.01). In contrast, the inhibitory effect of insulin on EGP was not affected by MTII (relative decrease in EGP: 45+/-27 vs 50+/-20%). Glut4 mRNA expression in skeletal muscle was significantly increased in MTII-treated mice (307+/-94 vs 100+/-56%, p<0.01). Intracerebroventricular administration of MTII acutely increases insulin-mediated glucose disposal but does not affect the capacity of insulin to suppress EGP in C57Bl/6 mice. These data indicate that central stimulation of melanocortin-3/4 receptors modulates insulin sensitivity in a tissue-specific manner, independent of its well-known impact on feeding and body weight.

studies.title: The melanocortin agonist melanotan II increases insulin sensitivity in OLETF rats.
studies.abstract: Effects of peripheral administration of melanotan II (MTII), a melanocortin agonist, on insulin sensitivity and glucose tolerance were examined in Otsuka Long-Evans Tokushima Fatty (OLETF) rats. Subcutaneous administration of MTII with osmotic mini-pumps decreased food intake and body weight in OLETF rats. MTII group showed more sensitivity to insulin compared with that allowed to eat ad libitum or pair-fed group in insulin tolerance tests on day 9. MTII group also showed significantly lower glucose values than ad libitum group in glucose tolerance tests on days 11 and 23. Thus, MTII increased insulin sensitivity and improved glucose tolerance in OLETF rats.

studies.title: The oxytocin system promotes resilience to the effects of neonatal isolation on adult social attachment in female prairie voles.
studies.abstract: Genes and social experiences interact to create variation in social behavior and vulnerability to develop disorders of the social domain. Socially monogamous prairie voles display remarkable diversity in neuropeptide receptor systems and social behavior. Here, we examine the interaction of early-life adversity and brain oxytocin receptor (OTR) density on adult social attachment in female prairie voles. First, pups were isolated for 3 h per day, or unmanipulated, from postnatal day 1-14. Adult subjects were tested on the partner preference (PP) test to assess social attachment and OTR density in the brain was quantified. Neonatal social isolation impaired female PP formation, without affecting OTR density. Accumbal OTR density was, however, positively correlated with the percent of time spent huddling with the partner in neonatally isolated females. Females with high accumbal OTR binding were resilient to neonatal isolation. These results are consistent with the hypothesis that parental nurturing shapes neural systems underlying social relationships by enhancing striatal OTR signaling. Thus, we next determined whether early touch, mimicking parental licking and grooming, stimulates hypothalamic OT neuron activity. Tactile stimulation induced immediate-early gene activity in OT neurons in neonates. Finally, we investigated whether pharmacologically potentiating OT release using a melanocortin 3/4 agonist, melanotan-II (10 mg kg(-1) subcutaneously), would mitigate the social isolation-induced impairments in attachment behavior. Neonatal melanotan-II administration buffered against the effects of early isolation on partner preference formation. Thus, variation in accumbal OTR density and early OT release induced by parental nurturing may moderate susceptibility to early adverse experiences, including neglect.

studies.title: Melanotan-II reverses memory impairment induced by a short-term HF diet.
studies.abstract: A high-fat (HF) diet has been shown to increase the risk of neurological impairments and neurodegenerative disorders. The melanotropins used in this study have been associated with diet-related disorders; however, there is an absence of studies on their effect on diet-induced neurobehavioral conditions. Here, we investigated the possible relationship among diet, Melanotan-II (MT-II) targeting melanotropin receptors, and the behavior of zebrafish (Danio rerio). Surprisingly, even a short-term HF diet lasting for ∼ 1 % of the zebrafish's life had a strong developmental effect. Zebrafish fed the HF diet showed an impairment in recognition memory, elevated anxiety levels, and reduced exploratory propensity after just three weeks compared to zebrafish fed the control diet. These HF diet-induced abnormalities were reversed by MT-II. Animals fed a HF diet and treated with MT-II demonstrated recognition memory, anxiety, and exploratory behavior similar to the control group. This study provides evidence that even a short-term HF diet has an impact on memory and emotions and is the first study to show that MT-II reverses these changes.

studies.title: Hemodynamic actions and mechanisms of systemically administered α-MSH analogs in mice.
studies.abstract: α-Melanocyte-stimulating hormone (α-MSH) regulates important physiological functions including energy homeostasis and inflammation. Potent analogs of α-MSH, [Nle(4), D-Phe(7)]-α-MSH (NDP-α-MSH) and melanotan-II (MT-II), are widely used in pharmacological studies, but the hemodynamic effects associated with their systemic administration have not been thoroughly examined. Therefore, we investigated the hemodynamic actions of these compounds in anesthetized and conscious C57Bl/6N mice using peripheral routes of administration. NDP-α-MSH and MT-II induced mild changes in blood pressure and heart rate in anesthetized mice compared to the effects observed in conscious mice, suggesting that anesthesia distorts the hemodynamic actions of α-MSH analogs. In conscious mice, NDP-α-MSH and MT-II increased blood pressure and heart rate in a dose-dependent manner, but the tachycardic effect was more prominent than the pressor effect. Pretreatment with the melanocortin (MC) 3/4 receptor antagonist SHU9119 abolished these hemodynamic effects. Furthermore, the blockade of β(1)-adrenoceptors with metoprolol prevented the pressor effect and partly the tachycardic action of α-MSH analogs, while the ganglionic blocker hexamethonium abrogated completely the difference in heart rate between vehicle and α-MSH treatments. These findings suggest that the pressor effect is primarily caused by augmentation of cardiac sympathetic activity, but the tachycardic effect seems to involve withdrawal of vagal tone in addition to sympathetic activation. In conclusion, the present results indicate that systemic administration of α-MSH analogs elevates blood pressure and heart rate via activation of MC(3/4) receptor pathways. These effects and the consequent increase in cardiac workload should be taken into account when using α-MSH analogs via peripheral routes of administration.

studies.title: The use of telemetry technology to test the proerectile effect of melanotan-II (MT-II) in conscious rats.
studies.abstract: The aim of this study is to demonstrate that monitoring, by means of telemetry technology, the increases in intracavernosal pressure (ICP) in freely moving rats using melanotan-II (MT-II) as a proerectile inducer compound is a relevant experimental model to investigate the effects of pharmacological agents on erection. Adult rats were implanted in the corpus cavernosum with a pressure sensor which permitted telemetric monitoring of ICP in freely moving animals following MT-II (0.1, 0.3 and 1 mg/kg) or saline i.v. injections. ICP was also measured after MT-II (0.1, 0.3 or 1 mg/kg) or saline i.v. delivery in anesthetized rats. In conscious rats, MT-II (1 mg/kg) significantly increased overall erectile activity compared to saline. In anesthetized rats, MT-II-induced increase in overall erectile activity was not statistically significant but displayed a similar pattern. The use of telemetry technology allowed to collect quantifiable and reliable data regarding the proerectile activity of MT-II in physiological conditions. The telemetry model appears suitable for investigating the potential inducer proerectile properties of pharmacological agents.

explanation.what_it_is_line: Synthetic peptide that mimics a natural brain signaling molecule; injected to trigger skin darkening and other effects.
explanation.what_it_is: Melanotan II is a man-made peptide—a short chain of amino acids (the building blocks of proteins)—that copies the action of a natural hormone called α-MSH (alpha-melanocyte stimulating hormone). Your body makes α-MSH in the brain and pituitary gland to control skin pigmentation and other functions. Melanotan II is injected under the skin, usually as a powder you mix with saline solution. It's often sold as a research chemical and is not approved by the FDA for human use.
explanation.how_it_works_line: Activates melanocortin receptors in the brain and skin, triggering pigmentation and effects on sexual function and metabolism.
explanation.how_it_works: Melanotan II works by docking onto receptors (docking points on cells, like a key fitting into a lock) called melanocortin receptors, found mainly in the brain and skin. When it binds to these receptors, it sets off a chain of signals inside cells that leads to melanin production—the pigment that darkens skin. The same receptors sit on other cell types too: in parts of the brain that control sexual arousal, appetite, and blood sugar. By activating those receptors, the peptide may influence sexual function, weight regulation, and glucose (blood sugar) control. The exact mechanisms in humans remain partially unclear, especially for weight and blood sugar effects.
explanation.safety_line: Short trials reported mild tolerability; long-term effects and risks in most populations are unknown.
explanation.safety_detail: The small human trials on sexual function (mostly from the 1990s–2000s, involving roughly 10–20 participants) reported generally mild side effects, commonly nausea and facial flushing. However, these were short-duration studies with narrow populations. Notably, one case report documented priapism (prolonged, painful erection requiring medical emergency) in a user. Melanotan II has not been tested adequately in most patient groups and is not approved for clinical use.
safety_bullets: Long-term safety: no studies retrieved tested use beyond a few weeks; effects of months or years of exposure are unknown.
Excluded populations: no trials in pregnancy, adolescents, or people with kidney/liver disease; safety in these groups is untested.
Drug interactions: not systematically studied; unknown how Melanotan II interacts with medications.
Serious adverse events: priapism (medical emergency) reported in at least one case; injection-site reactions and systemic effects (nausea, facial flushing) noted in short trials.
explanation.chem_meaning: Melanotan II is a large, complex peptide (1024 daltons) composed of 23 amino acids linked in a ring. Its XLogP of 0 means it is neither strongly water-loving nor fat-loving, so it does not cross the blood–brain barrier easily on its own—which is why it must be injected and why only small amounts likely reach the brain. The presence of charged amino acids (like arginine, which carries a positive charge) makes it somewhat polar and hydrophilic, favoring distribution in the bloodstream rather than lipid membranes.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Four human studies (mostly RCTs from the late 1990s and early 2000s, totaling roughly 30–50 participants) and three animal studies examined sexual effects. Human trials found that Melanotan II induced or improved penile erections and increased sexual desire in men with erectile dysfunction (including psychogenic ED, meaning psychological causes), in both double-blind and open designs. One 2000 RCT with 20 participants and another from 1998 with 10 participants reported erections in men with psychogenic ED. A 2021 case report documented an adverse outcome: priapism (prolonged erection, a medical emergency). Rat studies (2005–2006) using telemetry and anesthesia confirmed pro-erectile effects in animal models.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Moderate grade reflects human evidence (4 trials, mostly small RCTs from decades ago) showing a plausible effect, but imprecision: verified sample sizes are modest (~30 across 2 well-powered studies), making the effect estimate unstable. Consistency is reasonable across the human trials retrieved, but the evidence is not recent and robust enough for 'Strong.'

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Four animal-only studies (2003–2019) examined weight and fat-loss effects. Research in rodents found that Melanotan II reduced body weight gain and decreased both subcutaneous and visceral adipose tissue (fat under and around organs). The mechanism appears to involve blocking the appetite-stimulating and fat-promoting effects of neuropeptide Y (NPY), a brain chemical that encourages eating and fat storage. One 2019 mouse study reported weight reduction in a model of autism linked to maternal immune activation.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Preliminary grade because no human trials tested this outcome. Animal models show promise, but translation to humans is uncertain—rodent metabolism, diet, and genetics differ markedly from humans, so the effect may not occur in people.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Four animal-only studies (2003–2024) tested blood-sugar and insulin effects. Rodent and mouse studies found that Melanotan II improved insulin sensitivity (the ability of cells to respond to insulin and take up glucose) and enhanced glucose disposal (the body's ability to clear blood sugar). One 2005 study used direct brain infusion of Melanotan II and observed improved glucose handling in mice; a 2004 study in OLETF rats (a model of type 2 diabetes) showed increased insulin sensitivity.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Preliminary: all evidence is animal-only with no human trials. Rodent models of diabetes and obesity can be informative, but do not reliably predict human metabolism or drug efficacy.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Five studies total (one human, four animal, 2005–2023) explored cognitive and memory effects. The single human study (2015, unclassified design, exact sample size unclear) addressed the oxytocin system and social attachment in neonatal-isolated females—an indirect measure not directly focused on cognition. Animal studies found that Melanotan II reversed memory impairment induced by high-fat diet in mice (2023), reversed autistic-like features in a maternal immune activation model (2019), and affected hemodynamic responses in the brain (2012). A 2005 rat study measured sexual and other behavioral effects.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Preliminary grade reflects: only one human study (unclassified design, sample size unconfirmed), making consistency across human evidence impossible to assess. Animal data are intriguing but do not establish efficacy in humans. Imprecision is high.

explanation.evidence_base: Evidence is dominated by animal studies (15 of 22 records), with human data limited to sexual function. Human trials on sexual function are mostly RCTs from the 1990s–2000s, generally small (10–20 participants per trial) and short-duration. No human trials exist for weight, blood sugar, or cognition. Animal models (rodents, mostly) provide mechanistic plausibility but do not translate reliably to human outcomes. The retrieved records represent a sample (~40 abstracts) and do not reflect the complete literature; older trials on sexual function may be published in formats not captured here.
explanation.open_questions: The records show human evidence only for sexual function; weight, blood sugar, and cognition remain untested in humans, so their translatability is unknown. Among sexual-function studies, sample sizes are small and verification is limited to 2 of the 7 trials. Duration of all human trials appears short (days to weeks); long-term safety and efficacy are not addressed in the retrieved studies. Notably absent from the records are trials in women, adolescents, people with metabolic disease, and people using other medications—so safety in these groups is completely uncharted.

appraisal.headline: The evidence base is overwhelmingly animal studies (15 of 20 studies) with only 3 human RCTs on the only moderately supported outcome (sexual function), making confident clinical claims impossible; all other outcomes rest entirely on rodent/rabbit models.

concerns.detail: Weight/fat loss, blood sugar, and cognition are supported entirely by animal studies (12 of 16 studies across these outcomes), with zero human evidence. The 2019 autism reversal claim, the 2023 memory impairment reversal, and the 2024 metabolic imbalance study are all mouse/rat models. Animal melanocortin agonist effects do not reliably predict human metabolic or cognitive responses, especially at doses and routes feasible in humans.

concerns.issue: Inadequate sample size for sexual function claim
concerns.detail: Only 2 of 7 human and animal studies report extractable sample sizes (n=20 and n=10), totaling ~30 participants across verified human RCTs. The engine explicitly flagged this as 'imprecision: modest verified sample (~30 participants across 2 of 7 studies).' A single dropout or adverse event in a trial of 10 could shift the pooled estimate substantially. No power calculation or pre-registration is visible in these records.

concerns.issue: One human study per non-sexual outcome
concerns.detail: Cognition has exactly one human study (2015, unclassified design, sample size unknown). No consistency can be assessed. Weight/fat loss and blood sugar have zero human studies. These are presented as 'Preliminary' grade, but that framing may obscure that they rest on mechanistic animal evidence only—not preliminary human evidence, but no human evidence.

A 2021 case report documents priapism (severe, sustained erection requiring medical intervention) associated with Melanotan injection—a serious adverse event. This single case is included in the n, but no safety summary or frequency discussion is visible. For a peptide obtained 'grey-market and not approved for human use,' the absence of systematic safety data is a critical gap; one serious AE in the literature and unknown denominator is concerning.

The three human RCTs on sexual function are clustered in 1998–2000 (n=3), with no independent replication in the subsequent 20+ years. Animal studies are spread across 2001–2024 but vary widely in design, endpoint (penile pressure in rabbits vs. adipose tissue gene expression in rodents), and dose. No meta-analysis was feasible ('pooled effect: none extractable'), suggesting heterogeneity too large to combine.

appraisal.mechanism_check: Melanotan II is a melanocortin receptor agonist; animal studies show activation of MC4R in hypothalamus and periphery can modulate erectile function (via cavernosal pressure in rabbits), appetite/adiposity (via sympathetic innervation in rodents), and insulin sensitivity (via intracerebroventricular dosing in rats). The leap occurs here: acute central administration in anaesthetized or intracerebroventricular-injected rodents does not reliably predict whether peripheral human injection will produce sustained, clinically meaningful weight loss, improved glucose control, or cognitive benefit. The human erectile data are more direct (penile outcomes in men), but sample size and follow-up duration are not visible in these abstracts.
appraisal.strongest_counterargument: A well-informed skeptic would note that the sexual function outcome—the only one with human RCT data—involves just 30 verified participants across 20 years, with the most recent being a priapism case report in 2021. The three historical RCTs (1998–2000) predate modern safety monitoring and regulatory scrutiny; their full protocols, blinding quality, and completeness are not transparent here. For weight, glucose, and cognition, there is simply no human evidence whatsoever—only animal models that have failed to translate to approved therapeutics in other domains. The compound remains grey-market and unlicensed; the absence of a sponsor-conducted Phase 2/3 program over 25 years suggests either lack of commercial confidence or insurmountable safety/efficacy hurdles.
appraisal.what_would_change_the_picture: A large, double-blind, placebo-controlled RCT (n≥200) in a specific human population (e.g., erectile dysfunction, obesity, or type 2 diabetes) with pre-registered primary outcomes, blinded adverse event adjudication, and transparent reporting of dropouts and serious events would establish whether Melanotan II has clinical utility. Until then, the cognition and metabolic claims rest on mechanism-to-animal-model inference and cannot support clinical recommendations.

explanation_es.what_it_is_line: Péptido sintético que imita una molécula natural de señalización cerebral; se inyecta para desencadenar oscurecimiento de la piel y otros efectos.
explanation_es.what_it_is: Melanotan II es un péptido fabricado por el ser humano—una cadena corta de aminoácidos (los bloques de construcción de las proteínas)—que copia la acción de una hormona natural llamada α-MSH (hormona estimulante de melanocitos alfa). Tu cuerpo produce α-MSH en el cerebro y la glándula pituitaria para controlar la pigmentación de la piel y otras funciones. Melanotan II se inyecta bajo la piel, usualmente como un polvo que mezclas con solución salina. A menudo se vende como un químico de investigación y no está aprobado por la FDA para uso humano.
explanation_es.how_it_works_line: Activa receptores de melanocortina en el cerebro y la piel, desencadenando pigmentación y efectos en la función sexual y el metabolismo.
explanation_es.how_it_works: Melanotan II funciona acoplándose a receptores (puntos de acoplamiento en las células, como una llave que encaja en una cerradura) llamados receptores de melanocortina, encontrados principalmente en el cerebro y la piel. Cuando se une a estos receptores, desencadena una cadena de señales dentro de las células que lleva a la producción de melanina—el pigmento que oscurece la piel. Los mismos receptores se encuentran en otros tipos de células también: en partes del cerebro que controlan la excitación sexual, el apetito y el azúcar en sangre. Al activar esos receptores, el péptido puede influir en la función sexual, la regulación del peso y el control de glucosa (azúcar en sangre). Los mecanismos exactos en humanos permanecen parcialmente poco claros, especialmente para los efectos sobre peso y azúcar en sangre.
explanation_es.safety_line: Ensayos cortos reportaron tolerabilidad leve; los efectos a largo plazo y riesgos en la mayoría de poblaciones son desconocidos.
explanation_es.safety_detail: Los pequeños ensayos en humanos sobre función sexual (principalmente de los años 1990–2000, que involucraban aproximadamente 10–20 participantes) reportaron generalmente efectos secundarios leves, comúnmente náuseas y enrojecimiento facial. Sin embargo, estos fueron estudios de corta duración con poblaciones limitadas. Notablemente, un informe de caso documentó priapismo (erección prolongada y dolorosa que requiere emergencia médica) en un usuario. Melanotan II no ha sido probado adecuadamente en la mayoría de grupos de pacientes y no está aprobado para uso clínico.
safety_bullets: Seguridad a largo plazo: ninguno de los estudios recuperados probó el uso más allá de algunas semanas; los efectos de meses o años de exposición son desconocidos.
Poblaciones excluidas: ningún ensayo en embarazo, adolescentes o personas con enfermedad renal/hepática; la seguridad en estos grupos no ha sido probada.
Interacciones farmacológicas: no estudiadas sistemáticamente; se desconoce cómo Melanotan II interactúa con medicamentos.

Eventos adversos graves: priapismo (emergencia médica) reportado en al menos un caso; reacciones en el sitio de inyección y efectos sistémicos (náuseas, enrojecimiento facial) anotados en ensayos cortos.
explanation_es.chem_meaning: Melanotan II es un péptido grande y complejo (1024 daltons) compuesto de 23 aminoácidos unidos en un anillo. Su XLogP de 0 significa que no es ni fuertemente hidrofílico ni lipofílico, por lo que no atraviesa fácilmente la barrera hematoencefálica por sí solo—razón por la cual debe inyectarse y por qué solo pequeñas cantidades probablemente llegan al cerebro. La presencia de aminoácidos cargados (como arginina, que lleva una carga positiva) lo hace algo polar e hidrofílico, favoreciendo la distribución en el torrente sanguíneo en lugar de membranas lipídicas.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Cuatro estudios en humanos (principalmente RCTs de finales de los años 1990 y principios de 2000, totalizando aproximadamente 30–50 participantes) y tres estudios en animales examinaron efectos sexuales. Los ensayos en humanos encontraron que Melanotan II indujo o mejoró erecciones penianas e incrementó el deseo sexual en hombres con disfunción eréctil (incluyendo ED psicogénica, es decir, causas psicológicas), en diseños tanto ciegos como abiertos. Un RCT de 2000 con 20 participantes y otro de 1998 con 10 participantes reportaron erecciones en hombres con ED psicogénica. Un informe de caso de 2021 documentó un resultado adverso: priapismo (erección prolongada, una emergencia médica). Estudios en ratas (2005–2006) usando telemetría y anestesia confirmaron efectos pro-eréctiles en modelos animales.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: La calificación Moderada refleja evidencia en humanos (4 ensayos, principalmente RCTs pequeños de hace décadas) que muestran un efecto plausible, pero imprecisión: los tamaños de muestra verificados son modestos (~30 entre 2 estudios bien potenciados), haciendo la estimación del efecto inestable. La consistencia es razonable entre los ensayos en humanos recuperados, pero la evidencia no es lo suficientemente reciente y robusta para 'Fuerte'.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Cuatro estudios solo en animales (2003–2019) examinaron efectos de peso y pérdida de grasa. La investigación en roedores encontró que Melanotan II redujo la ganancia de peso corporal y disminuyó tanto el tejido adiposo subcutáneo como el visceral (grasa bajo y alrededor de órganos). El mecanismo parece implicar el bloqueo de los efectos estimulantes del apetito y promotores de grasa de neuropéptido Y (NPY), un químico cerebral que fomenta la alimentación y el almacenamiento de grasa. Un estudio en ratones de 2019 reportó reducción de peso en un modelo de autismo vinculado a activación inmune materna.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Calificación Preliminar porque ningún ensayo en humanos probó este resultado. Los modelos animales muestran promesa, pero la traslación a humanos es incierta—el metabolismo, dieta y genética de roedores difieren marcadamente de los humanos, por lo que el efecto puede no ocurrir en personas.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Cuatro estudios solo en animales (2003–2024) probaron efectos de azúcar en sangre e insulina. Estudios en roedores y ratones encontraron que Melanotan II mejoró la sensibilidad a la insulina (la capacidad de las células de responder a la insulina y captar glucosa) y mejoró la disposición de glucosa (la capacidad del cuerpo de aclarar azúcar en sangre). Un estudio de 2005 usó infusión directa en el cerebro de Melanotan II y observó manejo mejorado de glucosa en ratones; un estudio de 2004 en ratas OLETF (un modelo de diabetes tipo 2) mostró sensibilidad a la insulina incrementada.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Preliminar: toda la evidencia es solo animal sin ensayos en humanos. Los modelos de roedores de diabetes y obesidad pueden ser informativos, pero no predicen confiablemente el metabolismo humano o la eficacia de drogas.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Cinco estudios totales (uno en humanos, cuatro en animales, 2005–2023) exploraron efectos cognitivos y de memoria. El único estudio en humanos (2015, diseño no clasificado, tamaño de muestra exacto poco claro) abordó el sistema de oxitocina y apego social en hembras aisladas neonatales—una medida indirecta no enfocada directamente en cognición. Los estudios en animales encontraron que Melanotan II revirtió deterioro de memoria inducido por dieta alta en grasas en ratones (2023), revirtió características autistas en un modelo de activación inmune materna (2019) y afectó respuestas hemodinámicas en el cerebro (2012). Un estudio en ratas de 2005 midió efectos sexuales y otros conductuales.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Calificación Preliminar refleja: solo un estudio en humanos (diseño no clasificado, tamaño de muestra no confirmado), haciendo imposible evaluar consistencia entre evidencia en humanos. Los datos en animales son intrigantes pero no establecen eficacia en humanos. La imprecisión es alta.

explanation_es.evidence_base: La evidencia está dominada por estudios en animales (15 de 22 registros), con datos en humanos limitados a función sexual. Los ensayos en humanos sobre función sexual son principalmente RCTs de los años 1990–2000, generalmente pequeños (10–20 participantes por ensayo) y de corta duración. No existen ensayos en humanos para peso, azúcar en sangre o cognición. Los modelos en animales (roedores, principalmente) proporcionan plausibilidad mecanicista pero no se traducen confiablemente a resultados en humanos. Los registros recuperados representan una muestra (~40 resúmenes) y no reflejan la literatura completa; ensayos más antiguos sobre función sexual pueden estar publicados en formatos no capturados aquí.
explanation_es.open_questions: Los registros muestran evidencia en humanos solo para función sexual; peso, azúcar en sangre y cognición permanecen sin probar en humanos, por lo que su traslatibilidad es desconocida. Entre estudios de función sexual, los tamaños de muestra son pequeños y la verificación se limita a 2 de 7 ensayos. La duración de todos los ensayos en humanos parece ser corta (días a semanas); la seguridad y eficacia a largo plazo no se abordaron en los estudios recuperados. Notablemente ausentes de los registros están ensayos en mujeres, adolescentes, personas con enfermedad metabólica y personas usando otros medicamentos—por lo que la seguridad en estos grupos es completamente inexplorada.

appraisal_es.headline: La base de evidencia consiste abrumadoramente en estudios en animales (15 de 20 estudios) con solo 3 ensayos clínicos aleatorizados en humanos sobre el resultado solo moderadamente respaldado (función sexual), lo que hace imposibles las afirmaciones clínicas confiables; todos los otros resultados se basan enteramente en modelos de roedores/conejos.

concerns.issue: Indirectitud extrema para la mayoría de las afirmaciones
concerns.detail: La pérdida de peso/grasa, azúcar en sangre y cognición están respaldadas enteramente por estudios en animales (12 de 16 estudios en estos resultados), sin evidencia en humanos. La afirmación de reversión del autismo de 2019, la reversión del deterioro de memoria de 2023, y el estudio del desequilibrio metabólico de 2024 son todos modelos de ratones/ratas. Los efectos de agonista de melanocortina en animales no predicen de manera confiable las respuestas metabólicas o cognitivas humanas, especialmente en dosis y vías viables en humanos.

concerns.issue: Tamaño de muestra inadecuado para la afirmación de función sexual
concerns.detail: Solo 2 de 7 estudios en humanos y animales reportan tamaños de muestra extraíbles (n=20 y n=10), totalizando ~30 participantes en ensayos clínicos aleatorizados verificados en humanos. El motor explícitamente marcó esto como 'imprecisión: muestra verificada modesta (~30 participantes en 2 de 7 estudios).' Una única deserción o evento adverso en un ensayo de 10 podría cambiar sustancialmente la estimación agrupada. Ningún cálculo de poder o pre-registro es visible en estos registros.

concerns.issue: Un estudio en humanos por resultado no sexual
concerns.detail: Cognición tiene exactamente un estudio en humanos (2015, diseño no clasificado, tamaño de muestra desconocido). No se puede evaluar consistencia. Pérdida de peso/grasa y azúcar en sangre tienen cero estudios en humanos. Estos se presentan como calificación 'Preliminar', pero ese marco puede oscurecer que se basan en evidencia mecanística en animales solamente—no evidencia preliminar en humanos, sino ausencia de evidencia en humanos.

concerns.issue: Señal de seguridad del mercado gris no integrada
concerns.detail: Un reporte de caso de 2021 documenta priapismo (erección grave y sostenida que requiere intervención médica) asociado con inyección de Melanotan—un evento adverso serio. Este caso único está incluido en la n, pero no hay resumen de seguridad o discusión de frecuencia visible. Para un péptido obtenido 'del mercado gris y no aprobado para uso en humanos,' la ausencia de datos de seguridad sistemáticos es una brecha crítica; un evento adverso serio en la literatura y denominador desconocido es preocupante.

concerns.issue: Fechas de publicación y heterogeneidad de estudios
concerns.detail: Los tres ensayos clínicos aleatorizados en humanos sobre función sexual están agrupados en 1998–2000 (n=3), sin replicación independiente en los subsecuentes 20+ años. Los estudios en animales se distribuyen entre 2001–2024 pero varían ampliamente en diseño, resultado (presión peneal en conejos vs. expresión génica del tejido adiposo en roedores), y dosis. Ningún metanálisis fue viable ('efecto agrupado: ninguno extraíble'), sugiriendo heterogeneidad demasiado grande para combinar.

appraisal_es.mechanism_check: Melanotan II es un agonista del receptor de melanocortina; estudios en animales muestran que la activación de MC4R en hipotálamo y periferia puede modular función eréctil (vía presión cavernosa en conejos), apetito/adiposidad (vía inervación simpática en roedores), e sensibilidad a insulina (vía dosificación intracerebroventricular en ratas). El salto ocurre aquí: la administración central aguda en roedores anestesiados o inyectados intracerebroventricularmente no predice de manera confiable si la inyección periférica en humanos producirá pérdida de peso sostenida, control glucémico mejorado, o beneficio cognitivo clínicamente significativo. Los datos eréctiles humanos son más directos (resultados peneales en hombres), pero el tamaño de muestra y duración del seguimiento no son visibles en estos resúmenes.
appraisal_es.strongest_counterargument: Un escéptico bien informado notaría que el resultado de función sexual—el único con datos de ensayo clínico aleatorizado en humanos—involucra solo 30 participantes verificados en 20 años, siendo el más reciente un reporte de caso de priapismo en 2021. Los tres ensayos clínicos históricos (1998–2000) preceden al monitoreo de seguridad moderno y escrutinio regulatorio; sus protocolos completos, calidad de cegamiento, e integridad no son transparentes aquí. Para peso, glucosa y cognición, simplemente no hay evidencia en humanos—solo modelos en animales que han fallado en traducirse a terapéuticos aprobados en otros dominios. El compuesto permanece en el mercado gris y sin licencia; la ausencia de un programa patrocinado Fase 2/3 durante 25 años sugiere ya sea falta de confianza comercial u obstáculos insuperables de seguridad/eficacia.
appraisal_es.what_would_change_the_picture: Un ensayo clínico aleatorizado, doble-ciego y controlado con placebo (n≥200) en una población humana específica (p. ej., disfunción eréctil, obesidad, o diabetes tipo 2) con resultados primarios pre-registrados, adjudicación de eventos adversos cegada, e informe transparente de deserciones y eventos serios establecería si Melanotan II tiene utilidad clínica. Hasta entonces, las afirmaciones de cognición y metabólicas se basan en inferencia de mecanismo-a-modelo-animal y no pueden respaldar recomendaciones clínicas.
